summary: The prepared main checkout already contains the race-safety property requested by the issue, via merged upstream PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34274. load_jit builds in a UUID-private staging directory, loads the artifact before publication, and atomically renames the complete directory into an immutable cache leaf. Cross-node failure of flock can therefore cause duplicate private builds, but cannot make nodes rewrite the same object or shared library. No source correction was justified; this PR records the evidence and limitations.

tests.what_was_measured: 42 cache tests passed, including atomic publication losing a concurrent race gracefully and build-lock exclusion. This validates the checked-out cache implementation without relying on a shared-NFS flock for correctness.

A cold gfx950 Hadamard JIT attempt used the new private .staging-<uuid> path, then failed at compilation before GPU kernel execution because the CUDA-oriented source includes cuda_bf16.h, which is absent from the prepared ROCm toolchain. The failure was not ESTALE and did not involve in-place shared-cache linking.
The broad Hadamard matrix was stopped after repeated instances of the same compile-time missing cuda_bf16.h blocker; it was not treated as a numerical or serving validation.

remaining_limitations: Only one gfx950 host was assigned. The required two-node shared-NFS mount with node-local flock semantics was unavailable, so the original multi-node ESTALE failure was not reproduced end to end.
The reported CUDA DSA/NSA model and weights were unavailable; no full-model, CUDA, or distributed startup claim is made.

The gfx950 Hadamard kernel could not execute because its CUDA-oriented source requires cuda_bf16.h. This is a separate architecture/toolchain blocker and was not changed as part of the NFS-cache investigation.
Atomic rename behavior was validated on the local prepared filesystem and by focused regression tests, not on the reporter's particular NFS implementation.
